title: UK net migration falls to 77,000, lowest since 1997 excluding Covid pandemic – UK politics live
summary: Net migration fell in the year ending June 2026, according to the Office for National Statistics And this is how the ONS explains the fall in net migration in its report. Mainly it is because of a steep fall in the number of non-EU nationals coming to the UK, it says. This is a consequence of visa rules becoming much stricter. The last Conservative government first tightened the rules very significantly, and this crackdown has largely continued under Labour. Another factor is more Britons, and EU nationals, leaving the UK than entering or returning. While people arriving from outside the EU continued to add to the population, non-EU+ provisional net migration fell to 258,000 in YE [year ending] June 2026, down from 379,000 a year earlier. The fall in the net migration of non-EU+ nationals was the main reason for the latest decrease in overall net migration. It was driven by non-EU+ immigration falling by more than 100,000, while emigration remained broadly stable. Compared with YE June 2025, non-EU+ arrivals for work-related reasons fell by 45,000, asylum-related reasons fell by 19,000 and study-related reasons fell by 33,000. Continue reading...
